subject: Insurance
title: The Mississippi Flood of 1927
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Mississippi Flood of 1927.

hook.text: The 1927 Mississippi flood covered 27,000 square miles and displaced 700,000 people. Almost nobody had flood insurance.

buildup.text: The devastation was so total that the federal government stepped in with relief for the first time in US history.

discovery.text: The flood created the modern expectation that government—not insurers—should rescue disaster victims.

twist.text: This expectation created moral hazard. People rebuilt in floodplains knowing the government would bail them out.

climax.text: One flood reshaped the relationship between citizens, government, and disaster risk for a century.

punchline.text: 700,000 displaced, zero coverage. One flood changed everything.

quiz.question: What precedent did the 1927 Mississippi flood set?
options: Federal government first provided disaster relief
